test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 11 Aug, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Family Courts (Amendment) Act 2022 has amended the Family Courts Act, 1984. The Act allows ______ to establish Family Courts.
solution:
The correct answer is __**State Governments.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **State Governments** are allowed to establish **Family Courts** under the **Family Courts (Amendment) Act, of 2022.**
 
• The **Family Courts Act, of 1984 **was enacted to provide for the establishment of Family Courts for **speedy settlement** of family disputes.
 
• The Act applies to all states and Union Territories of India, except** Jammu and Kashmir.**
 
• The **District Courts **are already established under the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**, and they do not have the specific mandate of dealing with family disputes.
 
• The **Union Government **does not have the power to establish Family Courts as it is a subject under the State List of the Constitution of India.
 
• The **District Collector** is an administrative officer who is responsible for the collection of **revenue and maintenance of law and order **in the district. 
 
• Therefore, State Governments are the appropriate authority to establish Family Courts as they have the power to make laws on the subject of family disputes under the** State List of the Constitution **of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Family Courts (Amendment) Act, 2022 w**as passed by the Parliament of India on** 17th March 2022.**
 
• The Act was brought in to amend certain provisions of the Family Courts Act, **1984** to make it more effective and efficient.
 
• The Family Courts Act, of 1984 defines family disputes as disputes between** parties to a marriage,** between **parents and children**, or between other relations.
 
• The Act provides for the establishment of **Family Courts **in every city or town with a population of more than 10 lakhs.
 
• The State Governments have the power to establish **Family Courts and appoint judges** for a term of three years.
 
• The judges must have special **knowledge** in matters relating to family disputes.
 
• The Act also provides for the **appointment of counselors **to assist the parties in resolving their disputes amicably.
 
• The establishment of Family Courts has been a significant step towards addressing the issue of **pending cases** in the Indian judicial system.
 
• The Family Courts have been able to provide** speedy and effective justice** to the parties involved in family disputes.
